title: Why you can't catch cancer
body: Cancer starts from changes to genes inside a person's own cells.
In general, cancer is not contagious. It doesn't spread from person to person like a cold.
You can't catch cancer from someone else. Touching, holding hands, sharing meals and breathing the same air can't spread it.
So it's safe to hug, sit with and help someone who has cancer. Being close is a kind thing to do.
realWorld: When people don't know how cancer develops, they may think it spreads between people. That idea can cause fear.
model: This is a teaching model. The two dishes stand for two people's cells; real bodies are far more complicated.
